title: The problem git solves
definition: Picture a folder with essay_final.docx, essay_final_v2.docx, and essay_FINAL_actually.docx. You cannot tell what changed, you fear deleting any, and sharing means emailing copies. Git records your whole project over time: you keep one clean folder while git remembers every past version, so nothing is lost and you can always go back.

slides.caption: A version (a saved snapshot of your whole project)
slides.narration: A version (a saved snapshot of your whole project)

slides.caption: Your project folder and its files.
slides.narration: Here's your project — one folder holding all its files, the ones you keep editing.

slides.caption: Snap a version: photograph the whole folder.
slides.narration: Saving a version is like taking a photo of the entire folder exactly as it looks right now. That frozen photo is version 1.

slides.caption: You keep working; a file changes.
slides.narration: You keep working and change a file — styles.css gets edited. Your live folder moves on, but the photo you took doesn't.

slides.caption: Snap again — version 2.
slides.narration: Take another photo and you get version 2: the whole folder again, now with the edited file baked in.

slides.caption: Any version brings everything back.
slides.narration: Because each version is a complete copy, loading one restores every file at once — the whole folder snaps back to exactly how it looked then.

slides.caption: Three files, nearly the same name.
slides.narration: Here's a folder most of us know: essay_final.docx, then v2, then the one you swear is actually final. Three files, nearly identical names.

slides.caption: You can't tell them apart, or safely delete.
slides.narration: The trouble: you can't tell what changed between them, you're scared to delete any, and sharing one means emailing a whole copy.

slides.caption: Git keeps one clean file.
slides.narration: Git flips this around. You keep just one file in your folder, the clean copy you actually edit.

slides.caption: Behind the scenes, every version is saved.
slides.narration: Behind the scenes, git remembers every version you saved: a timeline of snapshots, so nothing is ever lost.

slides.caption: Jump back to any past version.
slides.narration: Need an old draft? Roll back to any past version on the timeline. One clean folder in front, the full history safely behind it.
